abstract: Peptide therapeutics are rapidly advancing in the biopharmaceutical field, but the high cost and low throughput of experimental screening call for more efficient discovery pipelines. We present an AI-driven framework for exhaustive hexapeptide screening that integrates physical interaction data with high-dimensional sequence features. The two-stage pipeline first encodes peptide-protein complexes using a fragmentation-based representation to capture local pairing patterns. Then, docking-derived binding energies are combined with a transformer-based model to learn sequence-energy relationships for each target. Applied to NRP-1, STING, and cGAS, the workflow achieved high hit rates and identified novel hexapeptides with micromolar binding affinities. By bridging physical modeling with enriched feature representations, this framework offers a robust, generalizable solution that accelerates peptide drug discovery.
